column1: You immediately regret phrasing your question in that particular manner. Marie doesn't seem offended, however.
column2: 你立刻後悔用那種方式問問題。不過 Marie 似乎並不介意。

column1: What do you mean, Marie?
column2: 妳這話是什麼意思，Marie？

column1: Well, ah, I--
column2: 呃，那個，我……

column1: Marie winks at you.
column2: Marie 對你眨了眨眼。

column1: There isn't a single patron in this bar who would sit still for being touched by a cop. Unless you count Marie, who is probably less of a patron and more of a solicitor.
column2: 這間酒吧裡沒有一個客人會乖乖讓警察搜身。除非把 Marie 算進去，不過她與其說是客人，不如說是個拉客的。

column1: Some of Willy's patrons. You're supposed to treat everybody equally, but it's hard not to think of these people as lowlife scum, the ones that give you so much grief on Friday and Saturday nights.
column2: Willy 的一些常客。你應該一視同仁地對待每個人，但很難不把這些人當成社會敗類——就是那些每逢週五、週六晚上讓你頭痛不已的傢伙。

column1: They're not talking. None of them would be the slightest bit willing to help out a cop.
column2: 他們什麼都不肯說。他們沒有一個人願意幫警察半點忙。

column1: As charming as Miss February 1969 may be, an officer of the law does not take other people's property.
column2: 1969 年二月份的封面女郎再迷人，執法人員也不能拿走別人的財物。

column1: It's a tool company's cheesy cheesecake calendar. Closer inspection reveals the date to be February, 1969. Well, that explains the girl's white lipstick and bubble hairdo, anyway.
column2: 這是一間工具公司出的俗豔性感月曆。仔細一看，日期是 1969 年二月。這下就能解釋照片上那女孩為什麼擦白色唇膏、頂著蓬鬆爆炸頭了。

column1: As much as you'd love to play a rousing round of pinball, you have other things to do.
column2: 雖然你很想痛快打一局彈珠台，但你還有別的事要做。

column1: It's an ancient pinball machine with real rolling digit counters, lame flippers, wimpy kickers, half-burned-out lights, barely audible bells and elliptical balls.
column2: 這是一台老舊的彈珠台，有著會滾動的實體計數器、鬆軟無力的擋板、弱不禁風的彈射器、燒壞一半的燈泡、幾乎聽不見的鈴聲，還有橢圓形的彈珠。

column1: You've got plenty, Officer. No need to take someone else's.
column2: 警員，你自己的就夠多了，不需要拿別人的。

column1: Billiard balls.
column2: 撞球。

column1: No need to go waving pool cues around. You've been issued more intimidating equipment.
column2: 不需要揮舞撞球桿。局裡發給你的裝備可威嚇多了。

column1: Pool cues of different lengths are in the rack on the wall.
column2: 牆上的架子上放著長短不一的撞球桿。

column1: You don't have time to play pool, Bonds.
column2: Bonds，你沒時間打撞球。

column1: The pooltable is covered with patches, tears, and cigarette burns.
column2: 撞球檯上滿是補丁、裂痕和菸疤。

column1: It's Wino Willy's, the most repulsive, sleazy, low-life bar in town.
column2: 這是 Wino Willy's，全鎮最讓人反胃、最低級下流的酒吧。

column1: You don't want that, Bonds.
column2: Bonds，你不會想要那個的。

column1: The sign says; "No gun rack, no NRA sticker, no service."
column2: 招牌上寫著：「沒有槍架、沒貼 NRA 貼紙，恕不服務。」

column1: I'll make you eat that, pig.
column2: 我要讓你把那東西吃下去，臭豬。

column1: The local working girl seems to recognize you. She looks familiar...
column2: 這位本地的應召女郎似乎認得你。她看起來有點眼熟……

column1: You smile at Marie. You don't want to let her know that you're shocked. `Her life is her own', you tell yourself. `I shouldn't be judgemental'. But when you look at her sweet face and remember, you wish it just wasn't true.
column2: 你對 Marie 微笑，不想讓她知道你其實很震驚。『她的人生是她自己的』，你告訴自己，『我不該妄加評斷』。但看著她甜美的臉龐，回想起種種，你多希望這一切都不是真的。

column1: Man, I knew I smelled pork.
column2: 呿，我就知道我聞到豬騷味了。

column1: Oink oink oink, piggy.
column2: 哼哼哼，小豬仔。

column1: What the #@$%&* do you want, PIG?
column2: 你這#@$%&*想幹嘛，臭豬？

column1: Yaaaaahoo! It's bar-be-que time!
column2: 呀呼！烤肉時間到啦！

column1: I'm gonna turn you into pork chops, boy!
column2: 我要把你做成豬排，小子！

column1: Looking for something, Sonny?
column2: 在找什麼嗎，Sonny？

column1: A word to the wise: The Lytton Police Department issues equipment to you so you can use it, not decorate your locker with it. Of course, you don't need your locker now...
column2: 給聰明人一句忠告：Lytton 警局發裝備給你是要你拿來用的，不是拿來裝飾你的置物櫃。當然啦，你現在也用不到置物櫃了……

column1: Don't leave now. You have to deal with those bikers.
column2: 現在別走。你還得處理那些飆車族。

column1: Your good friend SweatCheeks Marie is standing by the jukebox. It might be a good idea to talk with her and see what she knows about the drug problem in town.
column2: 你的好朋友 SweatCheeks Marie 正站在點唱機旁邊。找她聊聊、問問她對鎮上毒品問題知道些什麼，或許是個好主意。

column1: It will also give you a good excuse to go chit-chat with her.
column2: 這也正好給你一個藉口去找她閒聊幾句。

column1: Don't even think about it. You can't afford a new uniform, Bonds, and you'd have to burn this one if you sat on that stool.
column2: 想都別想。Bonds，你買不起新制服，要是坐上那張凳子，你這件恐怕就得燒掉了。

column1: These grime-coated stools make the ones in Carol's look positively upscale.
column2: 這些油垢滿滿的凳子，讓 Carol 咖啡城堡裡的凳子看起來都高檔多了。

column1: It's Wino Willy himself. Just looking at him makes you want to take a bath in disinfectant.
column2: 是 Wino Willy 本人。光看著他，就讓你很想去泡個消毒藥水澡。

column1: Good afternoon, Mr. Wily.
column2: 午安，Wily 先生。

column1: Good afternoon, Officer. Can I get you anything?
column2: 午安，警員。要來點什麼嗎？

column1: Willy smiles an oily smile that makes you want to wash your hands. His eyes are darting around like a paranoid poodle's.
column2: Willy 露出油膩膩的笑容，讓你很想去洗手。他的眼神像隻疑神疑鬼的貴賓狗一樣四處亂飄。

column1: Not today, thanks.
column2: 今天不用，謝了。

column1: I don't know nothin' about nothin'.
column2: 我啥都不知道，什麼都不知道。

column1: Nice, springy foliage.
column2: 好有彈性的葉子。

column1: That's one big plant!
column2: 這株植物真夠大！

column1: The plant doesn't respond, it only listens quietly. (Maybe it's a plant for the FBI.)
column2: 這株植物沒有反應，只是靜靜聽著。（搞不好它是 FBI 派來的臥底植物。）

column1: Ouch! Those plants are prickly!
column2: 哎唷！這些植物有刺！

column1: The attractive foliage probably makes your average suspect feel much better about his or her plight.
column2: 這些漂亮的葉子，大概能讓一般嫌犯對自己的處境感覺好受一點。

column1: The plants are grateful for your kind words. Usually, all they get is spit on.
column2: 這些植物很感激你的好話。平常它們得到的通常只有口水。

column1: You press the entry buzzer alerting the guard inside that you wish to enter.
column2: 你按下門鈴按鈕，通知裡面的警衛你想要進去。

column1: This is the button you push to gain entry to the jail.
column2: 這是進入看守所要按的按鈕。

column1: The management would prefer that you not muck about with the camera (even if you COULD reach it).
column2: 管理單位希望你別亂碰那台攝影機（就算你搆得到）。

column1: The surveillance camera allows Paul, the booker on the day shift, to make sure that nothing funny is going on.
column2: 這台監視攝影機讓白天班的建檔收押員 Paul 能隨時確認沒有異狀。

column1: It's your personal vehicle. It looks kind of strange here.
column2: 這是你的私人車輛。停在這裡看起來有點怪。

column1: It's your patrol car. Surely you recognize it by now.
column2: 這是你的巡邏車。你現在應該認得出來了吧。

column1: It's your unmarked vehicle.
column2: 這是你的無標誌車輛。

column1: Although an attractive gentleman, this guy's bad news. Now he can be bad news in jail.
column2: 雖然長得一表人才，這傢伙可是個麻煩人物。現在他可以到看守所裡繼續當麻煩人物了。

column1: You don't need to hold up the column, Bonds. It's sturdy enough.
column2: Bonds，你不需要撐著那根柱子，它夠堅固的。

column1: Decorative columns nicely frame the jailhouse door. No doubt the prisoners appreciate them.
column2: 裝飾性的柱子把看守所大門襯托得很美觀。囚犯們想必也很欣賞。

column1: Okay, I want the two of you to move over by the door...NOW!
column2: 好了，你們兩個給我到門邊去……馬上！

column1: You'd better enjoy this bust, you porcine piece of crap. Your time in this town is limited.
column2: 你最好好好享受這次逮捕，你這頭豬玀。你在這鎮上的日子不多了。

column1: Well, my day would be pretty dull if I didn't get opportunities to spend time with such special citizens as yourself. In this line of work a good laugh is always appreciated. Now put a muzzle on it, funny man.
column2: 是啊，要是沒機會跟你這種特別的公民相處，我這一天可就無聊了。幹這行，能笑一笑總是好事。現在給我閉嘴，幽默大師。

column1: You can't open it yourself.
column2: 你自己打不開這扇門。

column1: That's the remote-controlled door to the jail interior.
column2: 那是通往看守所內部的遙控門。

column1: Now's no time to be making an asphalt out of yourself.
column2: 現在不是在柏油路上出糗耍寶的時候。

column1: The asphalt serves as a fine driveway.
column2: 這片柏油地是很棒的車道。

column1: Boy, this guy's a mess.
column2: 天啊，這傢伙真是一團糟。

column1: Ok, buddy, your new room is waiting. Go on inside.
column2: 好了，兄弟，你的新房間在等你了。進去吧。

column1: Ah, a nice nap...(hic!).
column2: 啊，睡個好覺……（打嗝！）

column1: Ok, buddy, out of the car. You're home now.
column2: 好了，兄弟，下車吧。你到家了。

column1: Ok, Ossifer. Can do. No problemo. Always willing to co.. coor... cooper... do whatever you say.
column2: 好，長……長官。沒問題，絕對樂意合……合……合作，你說什麼我都照辦。

column1: Please stand over by the door.
column2: 請站到門邊去。

column1: Sshure thing, Ossifer...no problemo... just want to coorp... cooper... do what you just said.
column2: 當……當然，長官……沒問題……只想合……合……合作，照你剛剛說的做。

column1: Hmm, nice and sturdy. You wouldn't want to try going over that fence. Just thinkng about it makes you want to cross your legs.
column2: 嗯，堅固又牢靠。你不會想爬過那道圍籬的。光是想到就讓你雙腿發軟夾緊。

column1: That's the razor wire fence enclosing the jail's exercise yard.
column2: 那是圍住看守所放風場的刀片鐵絲網。

column1: You briefly consider picking a tulip to give to somebody special, but you prefer to keep up appearances and not be seen carrying flowers.
column2: 你一度想摘一朵鬱金香送給某個特別的人，但你還是決定顧全形象，別讓人看見你捧著花走來走去。

column1: Why do they even bother to plant flowers around the jail? The prisoners can't see 'em and the cops couldn't care less. There's probably some sort of asinine ordinance.
column2: 他們幹嘛還要在看守所周圍種花？囚犯看不到，警察也懶得在乎。八成是哪條蠢法規規定的。

column1: This guy's truly bad news. He'd cut your throat in a second, which is probably only twice as fast as he'd cut his own mother's.
column2: 這傢伙真的是個大麻煩。他會毫不猶豫地割開你的喉嚨，速度大概只比割他親生母親的快兩倍而已。

column1: Ok, get inside.
column2: 好了，進去吧。

column1: C'mon, outta the car.
column2: 快點，下車。

column1: Whoa! Tough guy. You screw up once, piggly-wiggly and I'll be all over you.
column2: 哇喔！硬漢啊。你只要搞砸一次，小豬崽，我就會盯死你。

column1: I'm not that kind of guy, but thanks for the compliment.
column2: 我不是那種人，不過謝謝誇獎。

column1: Shove it, ham hock.
column2: 少囉唆，火腿腳。

column1: Okay, Hoffmeister, or whatever your name is today. Stand over by the door and don't give me any trouble.
column2: 好了，Hoffmeister，或者你今天想用什麼名字都行。站到門邊去，別給我惹麻煩。

column1: Oh, yessir, pardon me, sir, right away, sir. Hehe...you ever hear the way a pig squeals when it's been stuck? It's like music.
column2: 喔，是的長官，抱歉，長官，馬上，長官。嘿嘿……你聽過豬被捅的時候怎麼慘叫嗎？簡直像音樂一樣。

column1: Don't bother, it has a perfectly good foundation and interior columns to help hold it up.
column2: 別費心了，它有很穩固的地基和內部柱子撐著。

column1: That's your new partner, Detective Laura Watts.
column2: 那是你的新搭檔，Laura Watts 警探。

column1: Hey, Sonny. I'll take Laurel and Hardy inside while you take care of the car and your gun.
column2: 嘿，Sonny。我帶 Laurel and Hardy 這兩位進去，你去處理車子和你的槍。

column1: Ok, Laura. Don't let Frick and Frack give you a hard time.
column2: 好，Laura。別讓 Frick and Frack 給你添麻煩。

column1: C'mon gentlemen. You don't want to keep a lady waiting, do you? Your castle awaits.
column2: 來吧，兩位先生。你們總不會想讓一位女士等太久吧？你們的城堡在等著呢。

column1: These are sidearm storage lockers.
column2: 這些是配槍置物櫃。

column1: Don't touch that concrete. You don't know where it's been.
column2: 別碰那塊水泥。你不知道它經歷過什麼。

column1: The sidewalk just happens to be conveniently located between the driveway and the jail entrance. Many an unwilling guest has marched down this very walkway.
column2: 這條人行道剛好就位在車道和看守所入口之間。不少不情願的訪客都曾被押著走過這條路。

column1: Aren't you forgetting something? Those police service revolvers are expensive. You shouldn't leave it behind in the locker.
column2: 你是不是忘了什麼？那把警用左輪手槍可不便宜，別把它忘在置物櫃裡沒拿。

column1: It would help to open the locker door before trying to lock up your revolver.
column2: 在你想把左輪手槍鎖進去之前，先打開置物櫃門會比較方便。

column1: Yup, nice and strong. Keeps perps in, keeps vandals out!
column2: 沒錯，堅固耐用。把嫌犯關在裡面，把破壞份子擋在外面！

column1: That's the barred office window of the Lytton County Jail.
column2: 那是 Lytton 郡看守所辦公室裝了鐵欄杆的窗戶。

column1: Nah. You're not in the mood for incarceration today.
column2: 不了。你今天沒心情去坐牢。

column1: Much as you expected, it's a jail cell. Many of Lytton's finest criminals have cooled their heels here.
column2: 正如你所料，這是一間牢房。不少 Lytton 數一數二的罪犯都曾在這裡蹲過。

column1: This is holding cell number two. Here you'll often find some of the less desirable elements of society.
column2: 這是二號拘留室。這裡經常關著一些社會上不太受歡迎的份子。

column1: It's another of the departmental holding facilities.
column2: 這是局裡的另一間拘留設施。

column1: Did you see the way he used your own weapon to kill you? Pretty resourceful. Now you know why lockers are supplied on the outside of this facility.
column2: 你有看到他是怎麼用你自己的槍殺了你嗎？真夠有辦法的。現在你知道為什麼這棟設施外面要設置置物櫃了吧。

column1: You shouldn't uncuff them until the booking process is complete.
column2: 在建檔收押程序完成前，你不該解開他們的手銬。

column1: You think about talking to him, but decide you've suffered enough verbal abuse for one day.
column2: 你考慮跟他說幾句話，但決定今天挨的口頭羞辱已經夠多了。

column1: Hey, you look real natural in there.
column2: 嘿，你待在裡面看起來還真自然。

column1: He responds with a comment which suggests a physically impossible position. It's not a very original suggestion.
column2: 他回了一句話，內容是叫你去做一個生理上不可能做到的姿勢。這提議一點也不新鮮。

column1: Alright, into the cells with the both of you.
column2: 好了，你們兩個都進牢房去。

column1: Move into the center of the room, please.
column2: 請走到房間中央。

column1: Please stand against the wall and don't move.
column2: 請靠牆站好，不要動。

column1: I'll keep an eye on the dogs, Sonny.
column2: 我會盯著這兩隻狗的，Sonny。

column1: Yeah, and you two can kiss my...
column2: 對啊，你們兩個可以親我的……

column1: Hey! Hey! Hey! Let's cut the spew, fella!
column2: 嘿！嘿！嘿！少廢話，老兄！

column1: Ok, there you go. Hope I didn't have those on too tight.
column2: 好了，這樣就行了。希望剛剛沒銬得太緊。

column1: Door's open, Sonny, any time.
column2: 門開著，Sonny，隨時可以走。

column1: He must have decided he didn't want to hang around here any longer. And you gave him just the opening he was looking for.
column2: 他一定是決定不想在這裡多待了。而你剛好給了他正想要的機會。

column1: You don't want to do that here.
column2: 你不會想在這裡做那件事的。

column1: Ya know, I'm not feelin' so good.
column2: 你知道嗎，我覺得不太舒服。

column1: Sleep it off, pal. You're going to need the rest when the judge gets ahold of you. He's got no tolerance for DUI offenders.
column2: 睡一覺消一消吧，老兄。等法官找上你的時候，你會需要這段休息時間。他對酒駕的人向來零容忍。

column1: I.. I'mm... Oh, crud, I think I'm gonna hurl.
column2: 我……我……喔，糟了，我想我要吐了。

column1: Okay, Mr. Barnum. It's time to weave your way to the cell.
column2: 好了，Barnum 先生。該搖搖晃晃走去牢房了。

column1: Mr. Barnum, please move to the center of the room so I can remove your cuffs.
column2: Barnum 先生，請走到房間中央，好讓我幫你解開手銬。

column1: Please move to the wall and remain still, Mr. Barnum.
column2: Barnum 先生，請走到牆邊，站好別動。

column1: Yyeah, thas a good idea, off(hic).. off(hic).. officher. Maybe it'll help steady this frrriggin' rroom.
column2: 對……對啊，這主意不錯，警……（打嗝）警……（打嗝）警官。或許能讓這該死的房間別再晃了。

column1: Step into the cell, please.
column2: 請走進牢房。

column1: Hey, Sonny. Aren't you gonna remove that guy's cuffs first?
column2: 嘿，Sonny。你不先幫那傢伙解開手銬嗎？

column1: Uh, oh yeah.
column2: 呃，喔對。

column1: Okay, you might want to rub those wrists to get the circulation going again.
column2: 好了，你可以搓一搓手腕，讓血液重新循環一下。

column1: It would be wise to leave this guy cuffed until you're ready to stash him in a cell.
column2: 在你準備好把這傢伙關進牢房之前，最好先讓他銬著手銬。

column1: This guy looks like bad news in the flesh. You know he would've wasted you given the opportunity.
column2: 這傢伙看起來就是活生生的麻煩人物。你知道只要有機會，他一定會做掉你。

column1: You consider conversing with the guy but decide it would probably be better to limit conversation to business-related topics only.
column2: 你考慮跟這傢伙聊幾句，但覺得還是把對話限制在公事範圍內比較好。
